item.title: Turning Implications Into Evidence: Actionable Solutions to Real-World Problems of Practice and Policy Based on Prior Academy of Management Publications
item.content:encoded:
Julian Birkinshaw, Western University

Thomas P. Lyon, University of Michigan

Denise M. Rousseau, Carnegie Mellon University

Majken Schultz, Copenhagen Business School

Mo Wang, University of Florida

Amid rising concern about the relevance of their contents, many scholarly journals mandate inclusion of a managerial implications section. This section may be relegated to a few paragraphs at the end of an article and comprised of speculative statements loosely connected to the paper's empirical or theoretical content. And there these unvalidated implications tend to remain, largely unaddressed in future research studies and having little relevance to practice or policy.

This special issue calls for original research that develops actionable solutions from previously published managerial implications. By developing actionable insights from underdeveloped or dormant implications, this special issue furthers the core function of any science: the development of a corpus of valid and reliable knowledge. An applied science has the added demand that knowledge be usable outside of academia.

Appel publié par Academy of Management Perspectives. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Developing actionable solutions from previously published managerial implications
  • Novel empirical or conceptual analysis of practice and policy implications
  • Real-world problems of practice and policy overlooked in managerial implications sections
  • Robust analysis providing specific guidance for practitioners and policy makers
  • Building on theory developed in Academy of Management journals to enrich and reveal nuances of their usefulness
